unsigned_ambiguity_and_zero_signature.evidence: AttemptRecord serializes failure_class, but ObservedAttemptRecord deserializes only stage and signature. Reconcile counts an unsigned ambiguity only when stage contains the substring ambiguous. The execution prefunded-balance failure record uses stage prefunded-balance-query-failed, so a transport-ambiguous failure_class is ignored. Execution genesis RPC failures return without writing a typed failure record after the start record. With no signatures and no counted ambiguity, reconciliation_result(0, 0) returns RECONCILED.

blocking_findings.impact: The frozen runtime can produce a reconciliation receipt whose result contradicts its accepted exact binding. That invalidates the independent-review gate and can mislead an operator about whether an interrupted attempt was fully classified.
blocking_findings.bounded_risk: The demonstrated paths occur before cryptographic preparation, PostgreSQL connection or writes, transaction signing, and on-chain submission. Reconciliation itself submits no transaction, and the existing journal blocks direct reuse of the same execution path. No Devnet effect or duplicate submission is established by this review.
blocking_findings.required_disposition: Materially revise the runner and author a successor binding. Reconciliation must deserialize and evaluate the typed failure fields, journal every relevant execution failure, and never derive RECONCILED from zero signatures alone. If a pre-effect failure is to receive a terminal non-PENDING result, bind a distinct proven-pre-effect outcome instead of treating absence of signatures as reconciliation. Add deterministic tests that parse actual journal records for transport ambiguity, unclassified failures, genesis failure, known pre-effect rejection, zero signatures, and signed pending/finalized cases.
